title: Mixed Conditionals / Nkọwa ndoro ndoro
bridge: N'igbo, ndoro ndoro adịghị enwe ụzọ ndoro ndoro nke ọma: anyị na-egosi ndoro ndoro na-akpọkpọrị ndoro ndoro na-akpọkpọrị ndoro ndoro. N'English, ndoro ndoro na-akpọkpọrị ndoro ndoro na-akpọkpọrị ndoro ndoro na-akpọkpọrị ndoro ndoro. N'igbo, ndoro ndoro adịghị enwe ụzọ ndoro ndoro nke ọma: anyị na-egosi ndoro ndoro na-akpọkpọrị ndoro ndoro na-akpọkpọrị ndoro ndoro. N'igbo, ndoro ndoro adịghị enwe ụzọ ndoro ndoro nke ọma: anyị na-egosi ndoro ndoro na-akpọkpọrị ndoro ndoro na-akpọkpọrị ndoro ndoro.
rule: Ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro. N'igbo, ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro. N'igbo, ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro. N'igbo, ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro.

concept_examples.text: If I had studied more, I would be more confident now.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na m were ụtọ ịrịba ọcha, a na-achịrị m nke ọma ugbu a.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪf aɪ hæd ˈstʌdid mɔːr, aɪ wʊd biː mɔːr ˈkɑːnfɪdənt naʊ/

concept_examples.text: If she were more organized, she would have finished the project yesterday.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ọ were ụtọ ịrịba ọcha, a na-achịrị m nke ọma ugbu a.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪf ʃiː wɜːr mɔːr ˈɔːrɡənaɪzd, ʃiː wʊd hæv ˈfɪnɪʃt ðə ˈprɒdʒekt ˈjestərdeɪ/

concept_examples.text: If I hadn't missed the flight, I wouldn't be stuck in this hotel.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na m were ụtọ ịrịba ọcha, a na-achịrị m nke ọma ugbu a.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪf aɪ ˈhædənt mɪst ðə flaɪt, aɪ ˈwʊdənt biː stʌk ɪn ðɪs hoʊˈtel/

concept_examples.text: If he were here, he would have solved the problem easily.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ọ were ụtọ ịrịba ọcha, a na-achịrị m nke ọma ugbu a.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪf hiː wɜːr hɪr, hiː wʊd hæv sɑːlvd ðə ˈprɑːbləm ˈiːzəli/

N'igbo, ndoro ndoro na-akpọkpọrị ndoro ndoro na-akpọkpọrị ndoro ndoro. N'igbo, ndoro ndoro na-akpọkpọrị ndoro ndoro na-akpọkpọrị ndoro ndoro.

levels.label: Mixed Conditional Type 1: Past Condition, Present Result
levels.translation: Ndoro Ndoro Nke 1: Ndoro Aha, Ndoro Nke Ugbu A

examples.original: If I had taken that job, I would be living in Madrid now.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf aɪ hæd ˈteɪkən ðæt dʒɒb, aɪ wʊd biː ˈlɪvɪŋ ɪn məˈdrɪd naʊ/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na m were ụtọ ịrịba ọcha, a na-achịrị m nke ọma ugbu a.
examples.note: Ndoro aha bụ aha (had taken) ma ndoro ndoro bụ ugbu a (would be living).

examples.original: If we hadn't argued, we would still be friends.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf wiː ˈhædənt ˈɑːrɡjuːd, wiː wʊd stɪl biː frendz/
examples.translation: Si no nos hubiéramos peleado, todavía seríamos amigos.
examples.note: El uso del adverbio 'still' (todavía) es común en este tipo de condicional mixto para enfatizar que el resultado persiste en el presente.

levels.label: Mixed Conditional Type 2: Present Condition, Past Result
levels.translation: Condicional Mixto Tipo 2: Condición Presente, Resultado Pasado

examples.original: If I were more careful, I wouldn't have made that mistake.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf aɪ wɜːr mɔːr ˈkerfəl, aɪ ˈwʊdənt hæv meɪd ðæt mɪˈsteɪk/
examples.translation: Si yo fuera más cuidadoso, no habría cometido ese error.
examples.note: La condición es presente (if I were) y el resultado es pasado (wouldn't have made). Nota que usamos 'were' para todas las personas en la condición, aunque sea informal.

examples.original: If she spoke English better, she would have understood the movie.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf ʃiː spoʊk ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈbetər, ʃiː wʊd hæv ˌʌndərˈstʊd ðə ˈmuːvi/
examples.translation: Si ella hablara inglés mejor, habría entendido la película.
examples.note: Usamos 'if + simple past' para la condición (presente) y 'would have + past participle' para el resultado (pasado). En español, ambos verbos van en subjuntivo/condicional.

examples.original: Had I known about the meeting, I would be there now.
examples.phonetic: /hæd aɪ noʊn əˈbaʊt ðə ˈmiːtɪŋ, aɪ wʊd biː ðer naʊ/
examples.translation: Si hubiera sabido de la reunión, ahora estaría allí.
examples.note: La inversión formal sin 'if' es más elegante y se usa más en contextos escritos o académicos. En este caso, la condición es pasada y el resultado es presente.

examples.original: Were I in your position, I would have accepted the offer.
examples.phonetic: /wɜːr aɪ ɪn jɔːr pəˈzɪʃən, aɪ wʊd hæv əkˈseptɪd ði ˈɒfər/
examples.translation: Si estuviera en tu posición, habría aceptado la oferta.
examples.note: La forma invertida 'Were I...' es el equivalente de 'If I were...' y se usa para registrar un registro más formal. Esta estructura es paralela a la inversión con 'Had I...'.

examples.original: If you hadn't lied, we would trust you now.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf juː ˈhædənt laɪd, wiː wʊd trʌst juː naʊ/
examples.translation: Si no hubieras mentido, ahora confiaríamos en ti.
examples.note: Este ejemplo muestra un uso común: criticar acciones pasadas con consecuencias presentes. El verbo 'trust' en presente simple después de 'would' es correcto porque expresa un estado general.

title: Advanced Passive Voice: Gerunds, Infinitives, and Modals / Nkwado ndoro nke ọzọ: Gerunds, Infinitives na Modals
bridge: Na Spanish, nkwado ndoro nke ọzọ na-emepụta na 'ser + participle'. Ọ bụghị ihe mere n'ihi na ndoro nke ọzọ adịghị egosi na modals ma ọ bụ na ndoro nke ọ bụghị n'ime ndoro n'ime (gerund / infinitive). Na English, nkwado ndoro nke ọzọ na-eme ka ọ bụrụ ndoro ọzọ: ị nwere ike ịnweta 'must be done', 'being done', 'to be done', etc. N'ime ndoro ndoro, nke a bụ 'debe ser hecho' n'ihi na 'has to be done'. N'ime English, ndoro ndoro na-eji na ndoro ndoro na-eji na ndoro ndoro na-eji na ndoro ndoro. N'ime Spanish, anyị na-eji ndoro ndoro na-eji na ndoro ndoro na-eji na ndoro ndoro na-eji na ndoro ndoro.
rule: Na English, nkwado ndoro nke ọzọ na-emepụta na ndoro 'to be' na ndoro ụbọchị, modals ma ọ bụ na ndoro n'ime ndoro, tụọnụ na participle. Na modals: modal + be + participle (bụrụ na 'must be done', 'can be seen'). Na infinitives: to be + participle (bụrụ na 'to be considered'). Na gerundios: being + participle (bụrụ na 'being watched'). Na modals perfect: modal + have been + participle (bụrụ na 'should have been informed'). N'ime ndoro ndoro na-eji na ndoro ndoro: 'This chair was sat on' (n'ihi na ndoro ndoro na-eji na ndoro ndoro). Kedu na ndoro ndoro ndoro na-eji na ndoro ndoro na-eji na ndoro ndoro. Na Spanish, nkwado ndoro nke ọzọ na-eme ka ọ bụrụ ndoro ndoro na-eji na ndoro ndoro na-eji na ndoro ndoro.

concept_examples.text: The report must be submitted by Friday.
concept_examples.translation: El informe debe ser entregado para el viernes.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðə rɪˈpɔːrt mʌst biː səbˈmɪtɪd baɪ ˈfraɪdeɪ/

concept_examples.text: The problem needs to be solved immediately.
concept_examples.translation: El problema necesita ser resuelto inmediatamente.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈprɑːbləm niːdz tə biː sɒlvd ɪˈmiːdiətli/

concept_examples.text: The package could have been delivered yesterday.
concept_examples.translation: El paquete podría haber sido entregado ayer.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈpækɪdʒ kʊd hæv biːn dɪˈlɪvərd ˈjestərdeɪ/

common_error.wrong: The problem must be solved *by us* immediately. (cuando no es necesario el agente)
common_error.correct: The problem must be solved immediately.
common_error.correct_alt: The problem has to be solved immediately.
common_error.explanation: Ọtụtụ ndị Spanish na-egosi na ndoro ndoro na-eji na ndoro ndoro na-eji na ndoro ndoro. Na English, ma ọ bụ ndoro ndoro na-eji na ndoro ndoro, ọ bụghị ihe mere n'ihi na ndoro ndoro na-eji na ndoro ndoro. N'ihi na ndoro ndoro na-eji na ndoro ndoro, ọ bụghị ihe mere n'ihi na ndoro ndoro na-eji na ndoro ndoro.

examples.original: The rules can be changed.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ruːlz kæn biː tʃeɪndʒd/
examples.translation: Las reglas pueden ser cambiadas.
examples.note: Usa 'can be' para posibilidad. Na Spanish, anyị na-eji 'se pueden cambiar'.

examples.original: The application must be completed before noon.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˌæplɪˈkeɪʃən mʌst biː kəmˈpliːtɪd bɪˈfɔːr nuːn/
examples.translation: La solicitud debe completarse antes del mediodía.
examples.note: 'Must be' na-emepụta na ndoro ndoro. Na Spanish, anyị na-eji 'debe + infinitive'.

examples.original: This issue should be addressed immediately.
examples.phonetic: /ðɪs ˈɪʃuː ʃʊd biː əˈdrest ɪˈmiːdiətli/
examples.translation: Este problema debería ser abordado inmediatamente.
examples.note: 'Should be' na-emepụta na ndoro ndoro. Kedu na ndoro ndoro na-eji na ndoro ndoro.

examples.original: The meeting may be postponed if necessary.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈmiːtɪŋ meɪ biː poʊstˈpoʊnd ɪf ˈnesəseri/
examples.translation: La reunión puede ser pospuesta si es necesario.
examples.note: 'May be' na-emepụta na ndoro ndoro. Na Spanish, anyị na-eji 'puede ser'.

examples.original: He dislikes being told what to do.
examples.phonetic: /hiː dɪsˈlaɪks ˈbiːɪŋ toʊld wɒt tə duː/
examples.translation: A él no le gusta que le digan qué hacer.
examples.note: Na Spanish, anyị na-eji 'que le digan', n'ihi na English na-eji na gerundio pasivo 'being told'.

examples.original: She is proud to be selected for the team.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː ɪz praʊd tə biː sɪˈlektɪd fɔːr ðə tiːm/
examples.translation: Ella está orgullosa de ser seleccionada para el equipo.
examples.note: El infinitivo pasivo 'to be selected' na-emepụta na 'ser seleccionada' na Spanish.

examples.original: The data needs to be analyzed carefully.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈdeɪtə niːdz tə biː ˈænəlaɪzd ˈkerfəli/
examples.translation: Los datos necesitan ser analizados cuidadosamente.
examples.note: 'Needs to be' + participle. Na Spanish, anyị na-eji 'necesita ser'.

examples.original: He admitted to being involved in the incident.
examples.phonetic: /hiː ədˈmɪtɪd tə ˈbiːɪŋ ɪnˈvɒlvd ɪn ðə ˈɪnsɪdənt/
examples.translation: Él admitió estar implicado en el incidente.
examples.note: El gerundio pasivo 'being involved' na-emepụta na 'estar implicado' na Spanish.

levels.label: Passive with Perfect Modals and Reporting Verbs
levels.translation: Pasiva con modales perfectos y verbos de reporte

examples.original: The thief might have been caught by the police.
examples.phonetic: /ðə θiːf maɪt hæv biːn kɔːt baɪ ðə pəˈliːs/
examples.translation: El ladrón podría haber sido atrapado por la policía.
examples.note: Usa 'might have been' para especular sobre el pasado. Na Spanish: 'podría haber sido'.

examples.original: The documents should have been signed yesterday.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈdɒkjumənts ʃʊd hæv biːn saɪnd ˈjestərdeɪ/
examples.translation: Los documentos deberían haber sido firmados ayer.
examples.note: Expresa crítica sobre una acción pasada no realizada. Na Spanish: 'deberían haber sido'.

examples.original: The president is said to be considering new policies.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈprezɪdənt ɪz sed tə biː kənˈsɪdərɪŋ nuː ˈpɒləsiz/
examples.translation: Se dice que el presidente está considerando nuevas políticas.
examples.note: Estructura con verbo de reporte: 'is said to be' + gerundio. Na Spanish usamos 'se dice que'.

examples.original: The lost city is believed to have been discovered in 2015.
examples.phonetic: /ðə lɒst ˈsɪti ɪz bɪˈliːvd tə hæv biːn dɪˈskʌvərd ɪn tuː ˈθaʊzənd ənd fɪfˈtiːn/
examples.translation: Se cree que la ciudad perdida fue descubierta en 2015.
examples.note: Pasiva con 'be believed to + have been + participio' para reportar hechos pasados.

title: Advanced Reported Speech / Nkwụ ụzọ ịnweta okwu
bridge: N'igbo, mgbe anyị na-eweta okwu n'ụzọ ịnweta, anyị na-eme ka ụbụrụ okwu na-eme ka o mere n'ụzọ dị mma ma ọ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ. Ma n'English, ọ dị mkpa ịnweta ụbụrụ okwu (backshift) mgbe ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ. 'She says she is tired' vs. 'She said she was tired'. N'English, ụbụrụ okwu ndoro ndoro dị mma ma ọ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ. 'will' na-eme ka o bụrụ 'would', 'can' na-eme ka o bụrụ 'could', na ụbụrụ okwu ndoro ndoro dị mma ma ọ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ. N'English, adịghị ịkwado subjunctive n'okpuru okwu ndoro ndoro dị mma ma ọ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ. 'Dijo que viniera' → 'He said to come' ma ọ bụ 'He said that I should come', na adịghị ịkwado adịbeụzụ ndoro ndoro dị mma ma ọ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ. 'today' na-eme ka o bụrụ 'that day', 'here' na-eme ka o bụrụ 'there'.
rule:
Maka ụzọ ịnweta okwu ndoro ndoro n'English (level B2):
1. **Backshift (ịnweta ụbụrụ okwu)**: Mgbe ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ, ụbụrụ okwu n'okpuru okwu ndoro ndoro na-eme ka o bụrụ n'ụzọ dị mma ma ọ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ. present simple → past simple; present continuous → past continuous; past simple → past perfect; present perfect → past perfect; will → would; can → could; may → might; must → had to (ma ọ bụ must mgbe ọ bụrụ na ọ dị mkpa nke ndoro).
2. **Mgbagha backshift**: ọ bụghị ịnweta mgbe okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ. ọ bụghị ịnweta mgbe okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ. 'He said he is ill' (ọ na-eme ka ọ nwere ike ịdị ọnwụ) ma ọ bụ 'He said he was ill' (ọ dịghị ike ịdị ọnwụ).
3. **Mgbakọta pronombres na possessives**: ịkpọpụta n'ụzọ dị mma ma ọ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ. 'I' → 'he/she', 'my' → 'his/her', etc.
4. **Mgbakọta adịbeụzụ ndoro ndoro**: today → that day; yesterday → the day before / the previous day; tomorrow → the next day / the following day; here → there; now → then.
5. **Okwu ndoro ndoro**: ọ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ, ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ bụrụ na ụbụrụ okwu a na-akwado na nke mbụ. 'if/whether' n'okpuru okwu ndoro ndoro, na okwu ndoro ndoro n'okpuru okwu ndoro ndoro. ọ dịghị ịkwado auxiliary 'do/does/did': 'Where does he live?' → 'She asked where he lived.'
6. **Okwu ndoro ndoro na ndoro**: ọ dị mkpa ịkwado 'tell/ask + object + infinitive': 'He told me to close the door.' ọ dịghị ịkwado 'that'.
7. **Ụbụrụ okwu modals**: 'would', 'could', 'might', 'should', 'ought to' adịghị enweghị ụbụrụ. 'must' ọ bụrụ na ọ dị mkpa ịkwado ma ọ bụrụ na ọ dịghị ike ịkwado n'ụzọ dị mma.

concept_examples.text: She said she had finished the report the day before.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ gwara na ọ gara n'ụzọ nke mbụ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃiː sed ʃiː hæd ˈfɪnɪʃt ðə rɪˈpɔːrt ðə deɪ bɪˈfɔːr/

concept_examples.text: He asked if I could help him with the project.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ pụtara ma ọ bụrụ na ọ nwere ike ịzọpụta ya n'ụzọ ndoro.
concept_examples.phonetic: /hiː æskt ɪf aɪ kʊd hɛlp hɪm wɪð ðə ˈprɒdʒɛkt/

concept_examples.text: They told us to wait outside.
concept_examples.translation: Ha kwuru ka anyị ga-eri n'ụzọ.

concept_examples.text: She warned that the meeting might be postponed.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ kwuru na ụgbọela nwere ike ịdị n'ụzọ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃiː wɔːrnd ðæt ðə ˈmiːtɪŋ maɪt biː poʊstˈpoʊnd/

common_error.wrong: She said me that she was tired.
common_error.correct: She told me that she was tired.
common_error.correct_alt: She said that she was tired.
common_error.explanation: N'igbo, 'gwara' na-akwado na object indirect (ọ gwara m), ma n'English, 'say' adịghị enweghị object personal; ọ dị mkpa ịkwado 'tell' mgbe a na-akwado onye a na-akwado okwu. N'ihi na 'said me' adịghị mma; ọ dị mkpa ịkwado 'told me' ma ọ bụ 'said' n'ọnụ ọgụgụ object.

levels.label: Statements with Backshift
levels.translation: Akwụkwọ ndoro ndoro n'ụzọ ịnweta okwu

examples.original: Paul said he was going to London the following day.
examples.phonetic: /pɔːl sɛd hiː wɒz ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə ˈlʌndən ðə ˈfɒləʊɪŋ deɪ/
examples.translation: Paul kwuru na ọ ga-abịa n'ụzọ nke mbụ.
examples.note: Ọ bụghị ịnweta ụbụrụ okwu: 'is going' → 'was going' na 'tomorrow' → 'the following day'.

examples.original: She mentioned she had already seen that film.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː ˈmɛnʃənd ʃiː hæd ɔːlˈrɛdi siːn ðæt fɪlm/
examples.translation: Ọ kwuru na ọ gara n'ụzọ nke mbụ n'ụzọ ndoro.
examples.note: El present perfect 'have seen' retrocede a past perfect 'had seen'.

examples.original: They claimed they would finish the project by Friday.
examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ kleɪmd ðeɪ wʊd ˈfɪnɪʃ ðə ˈprɒdʒɛkt baɪ ˈfraɪdeɪ/
examples.translation: Ha kwuru na ha ga-eme ka ụzọ nwere n'ụzọ nke mbụ.
examples.note: 'Will' se convierte en 'would' en estilo indirecto.

levels.label: Reported Questions
levels.translation: Okwu ndoro ndoro n'ụzọ ịnweta okwu

examples.original: She asked where the nearest bank was.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː æskt wɛə ðə ˈnɪərɪst bæŋk wɒz/
examples.translation: Ọ pụtara ma ọ bụrụ na ọ nwere ike ịzọpụta ya n'ụzọ ndoro.
examples.note: N'okwu ndoro ndoro, ụbụrụ okwu bụrụ n'ụzọ dị mma: 'was' n'ọnụ ego, adịghị 'was the bank'.

examples.original: He wondered if she had received his email.
examples.phonetic: /hiː ˈwʌndərd ɪf ʃiː hæd rɪˈsiːvd hɪz ˈiːmeɪl/
examples.translation: Ọ kwuru ma ọ bụrụ na ọ nwere ike ịgụ ya n'ụzọ ndoro.
examples.note: Maka okwu ndoro ndoro n'okpuru okwu ndoro, ọ dị mkpa ịkwado 'if' ma ọ bụ 'whether'.

examples.original: They asked us why we hadn't called earlier.
examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ æskt ʌs waɪ wiː ˈhædnt kɔːld ˈɜːrliər/
examples.translation: Ha pụtara ma ọ bụrụ na ha adịghị ịkpọpụta n'ụzọ.
examples.note: La pregunta original 'Why didn't you call?' se convierte en 'why we hadn't called'.

levels.label: Reported Commands, Requests and Suggestions
levels.translation: Okwu ndoro ndoro, ndoro na ndoro n'ụzọ ịnweta okwu

examples.original: The teacher told us to stop talking.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈtiːtʃər toʊld ʌs tə stɒp ˈtɔːkɪŋ/
examples.translation: Ndụmọdụ kwuru ka anyị ga-eri n'ụzọ.
examples.note: Maka ndoro, ọ dị mkpa ịkwado 'tell + object + infinitive'.

examples.original: She asked me to open the window.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː æskt miː tə ˈəʊpən ðə ˈwɪndəʊ/
examples.translation: Ọ kwuru ka m ga-ere nwọnwanyi.
examples.note: Maka ndoro, ọ dị mkpa ịkwado 'ask + object + infinitive'.

examples.original: He suggested going to the cinema.
examples.phonetic: /hiː səˈdʒɛstɪd ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə ðə ˈsɪnəmə/
examples.translation: Ọ kwuru ka anyị ga-abịa n'ụgbọela.
examples.note: Maka ndoro, ọ dị mkpa ịkwado gerund (suggest + -ing) ma ọ bụ 'that + should'.

examples.original: She recommended that we book early.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː ˌrɛkəˈmɛndɪd ðæt wiː bʊk ˈɜːrli/
examples.translation: Ọ kwuru ka anyị ga-eme ka ụzọ nwere n'ụzọ nke mbụ.
examples.note: Maka 'recommend', ọ dị mkpa ịkwado 'that + clause' n'ụzọ dị mma (subjunctive).
